report:
# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX Audit

**Evidence boundary.** This is a source-led audit, not a claim that every requested tool has public documentation. I found strong primary evidence for Sayaslicer, Woslicer III workflows, BMHelper, sound-slicer, BMS format constraints and keysound behavior. I did **not** find a usable public issue/discussion corpus for Woslicer II/III, nor evidence supporting a “top 10” Sayaslicer issues; the closed Sayaslicer issue index contains six issues and page 2 is terminal/empty ([closed issues](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed), [page 2](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed&page=2)).

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow actually evidenced | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sayaslicer | Open audio; add/move markers; optionally import MIDI/clipboard; preview; copy BMSE/iBMSC clipboard or keysound list; export keysounds; save project. Shortcuts include `Z`, `V`/`Shift+V`, `B`, `M`, `P`, undo/redo. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) | Zero-crossing reduces clicks but moves markers and can break iBMSC paste; very-large-file loading (>2GB) was a bug; Linux preview once failed on PortAudio. ([important notes](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes), [issue 5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5), [issue 12](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/12)) | Arbitrary snap 1/1–1/192; no published slice-count ceiling. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)) | Hundreds of rendered files via “export keysounds”; BMSE clipboard rounds to nearest 192nd, iBMSC preserves >192 resolution. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)) |
| Woslicer II | Legacy audio slicer; Sayaslicer explicitly targets drop-in replacement with similar behavior. Public guide evidence is for the III family rather than II. ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)) | Public, scrapeable bug/enhancement history not found; exact format/stereo/ceiling claims therefore not asserted. | Not published in sources found. | Legacy rendered WAV workflow; the guide describes “total output” from Woslicer and then BMSE placement. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| Woslicer III | Prepare empty BMS; either MIDI→BMHelper→DAW render→Woslicer clipboard read→set BPM→“総出力” (total output), or manually click cut points→total output; drag WAVs to BMSE and paste sequence. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Author calls this the most troublesome stage; file ordering and starting selection in Explorer/BMSE must match; a filename must appear in Woslicer or total output can be disabled; manual “btsugiri” is click-by-click. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Snap denominator/maximum not stated in the guide; BPM must be matched manually. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | “総出力” creates cut audio files, then WAV definition and sequence clipboard are pasted into BMSE. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) |
| BMHelper / Mid2BMS | Import MIDI; split/inspect; export transformed MIDI; render audio in DAW; copy “切断位置” (cut positions) to Woslicer; copy BMS sequence to BMSE; define WAVs. BMHelper also decomposes chords and reuses repeated pitches. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) | Multi-application handoff; direct text WAV-definition paste requires closing BMSE in the cited workflow; automation may not work, so manual btsugiri is fallback. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Not stated. | BMHelper clipboard/text plus Woslicer-rendered WAVs; files must be placed in BMS folder. ([BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) |
| PTSEQUENCER / DJMAX | Public source found is a community reference rather than a manual. It reports PTSEQUENCER’s DJMAX-era limit as 1,023 and DPC 2025 as 2,047. ([NamuWiki keysound](https://namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) | Hard resource ceiling; no public slicer UX/export documentation found in this run; do not infer non-destructive slices. | 1,023 reported for the older PTSEQUENCER; 2,047 reported after DPC 2025, not a slicer snap limit. ([NamuWiki keysound](https://namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) | Not established by a primary PTSEQUENCER manual in the sources found. |
| sound-slicer | Read TXT timing, slice WAV, emit BMS clipboard; expected folder has original files and a `wav` subfolder containing BMS plus numbered WAVs. Rhythmic mode makes one slice per MIDI event; melodic mode groups repeated notes (e.g., 500 notes→10 reusable slices). ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | Slight gaps can result; rhythmic mode does not deduplicate; both modes do not support BPM changes; old batch/PHP/SoX stack. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) | No snap ceiling; example explicitly says 1,000 notes→1,000 slices. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#miditext)) | Numbered WAV files plus generated BMS clipboard. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline

| Severity | Problem / evidence | Design implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Marker time and chart time can diverge: Sayaslicer warns zero-crossing moves markers and may cause missing keysounds or gamemode changes after iBMSC save. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)) | Keep audio edit boundary and musical/grid position as separate values; show both ms and grid coordinates and warn when an audio-only adjustment changes chart timing. |
| P1 | Woslicer requires BPM to be matched before total output; sound-slicer supports no BPM changes. ([Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#miditext)) | Dual ruler: source milliseconds plus beat/bar ruler with per-segment BPM map. |
| P1 | “Btsugiri” fallback is manually clicking all cut points. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Playhead-synced preview, zoom, keyboard nudge, and grid snapping should be first-class. |

### Interface / workflow

| Severity | Problem / evidence | Design implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Traditional workflow crosses BMHelper, DAW, Woslicer, Explorer and BMSE; WAV definition and sequence paste are separate operations. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) | One project and one undo stack; “Import to Studio” should create notes and virtual slices atomically. |
| P1 | File ordering is positional: Explorer sort order, drag start, and BMSE definition start must all agree. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Slice Library with stable IDs, preview, note count, source range and explicit mapping—not filename order. |
| P1 | Woslicer output may be disabled when its filename field is empty, with a workaround of clicking a black area. ([guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)) | Validate destination/source state visibly and never hide a required field behind focus behavior. |
| P2 | Sayaslicer needed a text-enlargement suggestion; macOS launch and Linux audio-preview issues appear in closed issues. ([issue 3](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/3), [issue 8](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/8), [issue 12](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/12)) | Test at 1380×860, support scalable UI, and show platform/audio diagnostics. |

### Settings / audio editing

| Severity | Problem / evidence | Design implication |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Zero-crossing is beneficial for click reduction but can invalidate high-resolution iBMSC positions; BMSE rounds to 192nd as workaround. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes)) | Make zero-crossing a per-slice override with before/after preview; preserve original grid position. |
| P1 | Existing tools expose useful controls—1/1–1/192 arbitrary snap, offset, fadeout, silent-tail threshold, partial BPM support—but these are split across export-oriented behavior. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features)) | Expose Snap, Sensitivity, Zero-X, Fade, Normalize and Auto-advance in a persistent toolbar/inspector; record values in project data. Sensitivity 0.55 is a proposed product default, not an observed legacy setting. |
| P2 | sound-slicer’s rhythmic method can create gaps and does not deduplicate similar sounds. ([README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#miditext)) | Offer overlap/tail policy and “reuse identical source interval” rather than forcing one file per event. |

### Backend / format

| Severity | Problem / evidence | Design implication |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | BMS identifiers historically expand from hex/limited base36 to base36; BMSE’s 2024 pilot adds case-sensitive base62 for 3,843 slots. ([BMS command memo](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm), [NamuWiki](https://namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) | Internal IDs must be unbounded/stable; export should negotiate base36/base62 and detect collisions/overflow before writing. |
| P0 | DJMAX-family references report practical keysound ceilings: old EZ2AC 255, newer EZ2AC 2,047, older PTSEQUENCER 1,023, and DPC 2025 2,047. ([NamuWiki](https://namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) | Validate target mode limits and offer reuse/packing suggestions before finalize. |
| P0 | Older engines can interrupt an in-flight sample on the same lane; reverb/effect tails therefore get cut, while Technika 2 is described as changing to non-interfering playback. ([NamuWiki](https://namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C)) | Mode-specific overlap simulator and tail-risk warnings; do not assume WAV correctness means target-engine correctness. |
| P1 | Large source handling was a real Sayaslicer bug (>2GB), and preview had a Linux PortAudio failure. ([issue 5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5), [issue 12](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/12)) | Stream/decode large sources, use proxies/waveform pyramids, and isolate preview backend errors from project editing. |
| P1 | Exported-file workflows create numbered files and folder management overhead. ([sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html)) | Store `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` virtual slices; export WAV/OGG only at finalize, with deterministic manifest and round-trip import. |

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer: keep these

**Keep from Sayaslicer:** cross-platform delivery; project save/load; drag/drop; arbitrary 1/1–1/192 snapping; offset; undo/redo; MIDI and marker clipboard import; BMSE and iBMSC export; base-62 toggle; silent-tail removal; fadeout; zero-crossing; preview and keyboard-first navigation. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#features), [shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts))

**Keep from Woslicer/BMHelper:** the fast marker-copy handoff from MIDI-derived timing; chord decomposition and repeated-pitch reuse; direct sequence clipboard; and mouse-based manual fallback when MIDI/automation is unavailable. ([Woslicer III guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))

**Improve rather than copy:** Sayaslicer’s own warning shows that zero-crossing can change the chart-facing marker. DJMax Studio should keep a musical marker immutable while allowing a separate audio boundary to move. ([README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes))

## 4. Top 10 recommendations, prioritized

1. **P0 — Non-destructive virtual slices as the canonical model.** Eliminates numbered-WAV churn evidenced by sound-slicer/BMHelper workflows. ([sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html))
2. **P0 — Atomic “Import to Studio.”** Replace the multi-app, multi-clipboard handoff. ([Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
3. **P0 — Dual timeline.** Waveform/source-ms ruler below, chart/bar/beat ruler above, synchronized playhead; BPM map handles the documented BPM limitation. ([Sayaslicer](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#planned-features), [sound-slicer](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#miditext))
4. **P0 — Stable IDs plus export preflight.** Detect base36/base62 overflow, target limits and duplicate/collision risks before files are emitted. ([BMS memo](https://hitkey.nekokan.dyndns.info/cmds.htm), [NamuWiki](https://namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C))
5. **P0 — Engine-mode playback simulation.** BMS/DJMAX/TECHNIKA modes should visualize same-lane interruption versus non-interfering playback and reverb-tail truncation. ([NamuWiki](https://namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C))
6. **P1 — Per-slice audio inspector.** Zero-X, Fade, Normalize, tail policy and preview, with non-destructive overrides. Zero-crossing’s documented side effect makes global-only control unsafe. ([Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#important-notes))
7. **P1 — Persistent snap and auto-advance controls.** Offer 1/4 through 1/192 plus arbitrary values, Grid/Beat/Off advance, and keyboard shortcuts modeled on Sayaslicer. ([Sayaslicer shortcuts](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer#keyboard-shortcuts))
8. **P1 — Slice Library.** Searchable rows with source range, chart position, target ID, notes using it, preview and “reuse”; this directly removes Explorer sort-order coupling. ([Woslicer guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/))
9. **P1 — Large-file and resilient preview architecture.** Stream sources and waveform proxies; surface PortAudio/device errors without blocking editing. ([issue 5](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/5), [issue 12](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues/12))
10. **P2 — Finalize/export manifest and round trip.** Emit WAV/OGG only on finalize, write a manifest linking every target ID to source range, and re-import without losing virtual boundaries. This is the clean replacement for numbered WAV folders described in the legacy workflow. ([sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer#project-layout))

### Not established from public sources in this crawl

No sourced claim is made here for Sayaslicer settings named **Sensitivity 0.55**, Woslicer’s exact snap denominator, stereo/codec ceilings, a PTSEQUENCER user manual, or YouTube-comment pain points. Those should be validated with product telemetry or direct user interviews rather than filled in speculatively.
